Node 22 built-ins only, no npm install. READ FIRST: /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/.team/notes/spec.md (final spec; the "Booking rules" section and the "Before sending any reply ... reads the whole request body" line are yours), /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/.team/notes/backend-api.md, and the shared helper /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/test/helpers/server.mjs (exports useServer({before,after}) -> ctx with ctx.port filled in `before`; request(port,{method,path,headers,body}); postBooking(port, obj|string|Buffer, headers = {'Content-Type':'application/json'}); rawRequest(port, rawStringOrBuffer) -> whole raw response (latin1 string) until the server closes; VALID_BOOKING = {room:'Aurora',title:'Standup',date:'2026-11-03',start:'09:00',end:'10:00'}). Do not edit server.mjs or the helper. Code under test: /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/server.mjs (read for understanding; the SPEC is the authority). Create exactly two files: 1. /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/test/booking-rules.test.mjs — rules 4-10 and field handling. 2. /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/test/request-body.test.mjs — rules 1-3, sizes, encodings, full body reading. Files under 400 lines, functions under 50 lines; table-driven (one `test` per case, named after the case). No console.log. Bookings persist in the shared server, so make valid-case tests use unique (room,date,time) combos that never collide, or use a separate useServer per describe. Valid (201): '2000-01-01', '2099-12-31', '2000-02-29', '2004-02-29', '2096-02-29', '2026-04-30', '2026-12-31'. - start invalid (400 start): '24:00', '23:60', '9:00', '09:0', '09:00:00', ' 09:00', '09:00 ', '09h00', '０９:００', '-1:00', 900, null, missing, ''. Valid start '00:00'. - end invalid (400 end) with valid start: '24:00', '23:60', '9:30', ' 10:00', '10:00 ', null, missing. Valid end '23:59' (e.g. 23:00-23:59). - order (400 order): end == start ('10:00','10:00'); end < start ('10:00','09:59'); '00:00'-'00:00'. Valid: '00:00'-'00:01', '23:58'-'23:59'. - Rule order (first failing rule decides): all fields wrong → room message; room ok + title/date/start/end wrong → title; then date; then start; then end; start ok + end wrong format and before start (e.g. start '10:00', end '9:00') → end message, not order; a booking that would overlap an existing one but has an invalid end → 400 end, not 409. - Other keys ignored: body with extra keys id:99, extra:'x', __proto__-free → 201 whose body has exactly the 6 keys and an id assigned by the server (not 99). - Overlap (use one room/date dedicated to this describe, existing A = 09:00-10:00): 10:00-11:00 → 201 (touching after); 08:00-09:00 → 201 (touching before); 09:59-10:30 → 409 'room is already booked from 09:00 to 10:00'; 08:30-09:01 → 409; 09:00-10:00 → 409; 09:15-09:45 → 409; 08:30-10:30 → 409 (hmm: careful, this would also overlap the touching bookings 10:00-11:00 / 08:00-09:00 if those were created; design the times so each assertion's expected earliest booking is correct, or use separate dates per case). Same time in another room → 201; same room on another date → 201. - Earliest overlap reported: on a fresh date, create B 11:00-12:00 FIRST, then A 09:00-10:00, then C 13:00-14:00 (so id order differs from start order); POST 08:00-15:00 → 409 'room is already booked from 09:00 to 10:00'; POST 11:30-13:30 → 409 'room is already booked from 11:00 to 12:00'. - The 201 reply for a valid booking deepEqual {id:, room, title, date, start, end} with fields unchanged (except trimmed title). request-body.test.mjs: - Rule 1 → 415 {error:'content type must be application/json'}: no Content-Type header; 'text/plain'; 'application/jsonx'; 'application/json-patch+json'; 'application/ json'; 'application/json,text/plain'; 'json'; ''. Accepted (201 with a valid body): 'application/json', 'Application/JSON', 'APPLICATION/JSON; charset=utf-8', 'application/json;charset=latin1', 'application/json ; x=y'. Via rawRequest (to control exact bytes, with Content-Length and 'Connection: close'): media type with a trailing TAB before ';' ("application/json\t; charset=utf-8") → 201; header value 'application/json' followed by byte 0xA0 (NBSP, send as Buffer) → 415 (only spaces and tabs are removed, not other whitespace); 'application/json\u000b' (vertical tab) is likely rejected by the HTTP parser — skip it. - Rule order 1-3: wrong content type + 20000-byte body → 415; wrong content type + invalid JSON → 415; correct type + 10001-byte invalid JSON → 413 {error:'body too large'}; correct type + 10001-byte valid booking (padded with spaces) → 413. - Size boundary: a valid booking JSON padded with trailing spaces to exactly 10000 bytes → 201; exactly 10001 bytes → 413. Byte counting, not characters: a body whose JSON contains an ignored key with 5000 × 'é' (2 bytes each) so it is > 10000 bytes but < 10000 UTF-16 chars → 413; and one with 4900 × 'é' and total bytes <= 10000 → 201. Chunked body (no Content-Length; write in several chunks with Transfer-Encoding: chunked via rawRequest or http.request writing pieces) totalling 10001 bytes → 413, and 10000 → 201. - Rule 3 → 400 {error:'body must be a JSON object'}: '' (empty), ' ', 'nul', 'null', '[]', '[{}]', '"s"', '1', 'true', '{', '{"room":"Aurora",}', and a valid booking JSON prefixed with the UTF-8 BOM bytes EF BB BF (Buffer). Invalid UTF-8 is not an error by itself: a valid booking whose title bytes contain 0xFF (build a Buffer: JSON text with title "A" + 0xFF byte + "B") → 201 and stored title exactly 'A�B'. UTF-8 title 'Café ☕' → 201 stored exactly. - Whole body read before replying: using rawRequest with a keep-alive first request and a second pipelined request, e.g. Buffer.concat of [`POST /api/bookings HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\nContent-Type: text/plain\r\nContent-Length: 50000\r\n\r\n` + 50000 bytes, `GET /api/rooms HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n`] → the raw response contains 'HTTP/1.1 415' followed later by 'HTTP/1.1 200' and the rooms JSON. Same with 50000-byte JSON-typed body → 413 then 200. Same with a 30000-byte body on GET /nope → 404 then 200, and on POST /api/rooms → 405 then 200. Also a plain http.request POST with a 2 MB body and wrong content type receives status 415 and the full error body (no ECONNRESET/EPIPE). - Server still alive at the end (GET /api/rooms 200). Final message: files, number of tests, pass/fail, any spec violation (request, expected, actual). Keep it short.

content.content: 1 # Spec — meeting-room booking app (owner: supervisor, verbatim user requirements; FINAL, do not ask questions) 2 3 Constraints: Node.js built-ins only (no npm install). Node v22. Tests use node:test. Do not use the Fable model. 4 5 Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. 6 7 ## Server 8 - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. 9 - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. Both test files are written. `booking-rules.test.mjs` is green, but `request-body.test.mjs` is not: its last run had 4 failures. After that run the Bash tool was denied permission, so I stopped. I did not work around the denial, and I never re-ran the file after the fixes below.

**Files (both under 400 lines)**

- `/root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/test/request-body.test.mjs`: about 252 lines.

I did not touch `server.mjs` or the helper. The `tdd-workflow` skill is not in the skill list, so I skipped it.

**Test runs**
- **`booking-rules.test.mjs`:** 112 tests, 112 pass, 0 fail. The server showed no spec violations in this file.
- **`request-body.test.mjs`:** 48 tests, 44 pass, 4 fail. The failures are:
  - **"right type + 10001-byte non-object -> 413":** this was my test bug. The body was 10000 bytes, not 10001, so the server correctly answered 400. I changed it to 9999 spaces, and it is not re-run.
  - **Raw `rawRequest` cases, "accepted: TAB before ; (raw)", "accepted: leading TAB and spaces (raw)", and the 10000-byte chunked body:** the status parsed as NaN, so no `HTTP/1.1 NNN` line came back, probably an empty response. I don't yet know whether my raw request builder is wrong or the server mishandles these cases.
  - **Not diagnosed:** the same raw builder passes for the 0xA0 case, and a 10001-byte chunked body gets its 413, so the builder itself works.

I ran a `sed` that adds the raw response as the assertion message to those 201 checks. It was denied, so nothing was applied.

**What you need to do**
- Run `cd /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc && node --test test/request-body.test.mjs`.
- If the three raw tests still fail, add `raw` as the assertion message to see what came back, then decide whether it is a server spec violation or a test bug.
- If you restore Bash permission, I can finish this.

I have no confirmed server spec violation so far.
